records.source: Καὶ εἶδον ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὸ ἀρνίον μίαν ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ σφραγίδων, καὶ ἤκουσα ἑνὸς ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων λέγοντος ὡς φωνῇ βροντῆς· Ἔρχου.
records.gloss: And I saw when opened the Lamb one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures saying as with a voice of thunder: Come.
pieces: I looked on as the Lamb broke open one of the seven seals. One of the four living creatures cried out with a voice like thunder, and I heard it say, "Come!"

L.1: And I saw when the Lamb opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures saying, as with a voice of thunder, "Come!"

R.1: Then I watched the Lamb open the first of the seven seals. I heard one of the four living creatures shout with a voice like thunder. It said, "Come!"

decisions.choice: one of the seven seals: the first
decisions.reason: μίαν "one" is used for "first", as often in the Greek of the New Testament (compare Mark 16:2). The next seals are counted second, third and so on.

decisions.choice: Come! A call to the rider, not to John
alternatives: Come and see, said to John
decisions.reason: The creature calls the horse and rider to come out, and each one goes out (6:2, 4, 5, 8). Some manuscripts add "and see", which makes the call an invitation to John. The SBLGNT reads only "Come". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: four horses: Zechariah's visions
decisions.reason: Zechariah saw horses of different colors sent out to patrol the earth (Zechariah 1:8-11) and four chariots drawn by red, black, white and dappled horses, the four winds of heaven (Zechariah 6:1-8). John's four horsemen draw on these pictures. They also follow the order of the troubles Jesus foretold: war, famine, plague and persecution (Mark 13:7-9; Luke 21:9-12).

records.heading: The first four seals

records.source: καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος λευκός, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἔχων τόξον, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ στέφανος, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν νικῶν καὶ ἵνα νικήσῃ.
records.gloss: And I saw, and behold a horse white, and the [one] sitting on it having a bow, and was given to him a crown, and he went out conquering and so that he might conquer.
pieces: I looked, and I saw a white horse. The one who sat on it carried a bow. A crown was given to him, and out he went, winning victories and set on winning more.

L.2: And I looked, and look, a white horse, and the one seated on it had a bow, and a crown was given to him, and he went out conquering and to conquer.

R.2: I looked and saw a white horse. The rider had a bow, and he received a crown. He rode out to win battle after battle.

decisions.choice: the rider on the white horse: conquest, the first of four plagues
alternatives: Christ, or the gospel going out to win the world
a false Christ who imitates him
decisions.reason: Christ rides a white horse in 19:11, and some take this rider to be him or the spread of the gospel. But this rider is one of four sent out by the same call, and the other three bring war, famine and death. He has a bow, not the sword of Christ's mouth (19:15), and he is given his crown. So he most likely stands for conquest and the power of invading armies; the white horse may make him look like a victor, or like Christ. The bow may recall the Parthian mounted archers who threatened Rome's eastern border.

decisions.choice: was given: God permits it
decisions.reason: "Was given" leaves the giver unnamed, but in Revelation it is God who allows the riders to act (compare 6:4, 8; 9:1-5; 13:5-7). Even the forces of war and death act only within the limits he sets.

decisions.choice: conquering (L); winning victories (B); win battle after battle (R)
decisions.reason: νικῶν is the verb rendered "overcome" in the letters. Here its subject wins by force of arms, so the levels use words of military conquest.

records.source: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν δευτέραν, ἤκουσα τοῦ δευτέρου ζῴου λέγοντος· Ἔρχου.
records.gloss: And when he opened the seal the second, I heard the second living creature saying: Come.
pieces: The Lamb broke the second seal, and I heard the second living creature say, "Come!"

L.3: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying, "Come!"

R.3: When the Lamb opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature say, "Come!"

decisions.choice: the pattern repeats
decisions.reason: Each of the first four seals follows the same pattern: the Lamb opens a seal, one of the living creatures calls "Come!", and a horse and rider go out. See the notes on 6:1.

decisions.choice: the Lamb (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Lamb, who opens every seal (6:1).

records.source: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἄλλος ἵππος πυρρός, καὶ τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἐδόθη αὐτῷ λαβεῖν τὴν εἰρήνην ἐκ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἵνα ἀλλήλους σφάξουσιν, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ μάχαιρα μεγάλη.
records.gloss: And went out another horse fiery-red, and to the [one] sitting on it was given to him to take the peace from the earth, and that one another they will slaughter, and was given to him a sword great.
pieces: Out came another horse, red as fire. The one riding it was permitted to take peace from the earth and to make people slaughter each other, and a great sword was put in his hand.

L.4: And another horse went out, fiery red, and to the one seated on it, it was given to him to take peace from the earth, and that [people] would slaughter one another, and a great sword was given to him.

R.4: Another horse came out. It was bright red. Its rider was allowed to take peace away from the earth, so that people killed each other. He was given a large sword.

decisions.choice: the red horse: war and bloodshed
decisions.reason: Red is the color of fire and blood. The rider takes away peace, so that people slaughter one another, which may mean civil strife as well as war between nations. σφάξουσιν is the word used of the slaughtered Lamb (5:6, 9): people now do to one another what was done to him.

decisions.choice: was given: God permits it
decisions.reason: "Was given" leaves the giver unnamed, but in Revelation it is God who allows the riders to act (compare 6:4, 8; 9:1-5; 13:5-7). Even the forces of war and death act only within the limits he sets.

decisions.choice: people
decisions.reason: The Greek has only "they will slaughter one another". Every level supplies who: the people of the earth.

records.source: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξε τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν τρίτην, ἤκουσα τοῦ τρίτου ζῴου λέγοντος· Ἔρχου.
records.gloss: And when he opened the seal the third, I heard the third living creature saying: Come.
pieces: The Lamb broke the third seal, and I heard the third living creature say, "Come!"

L.5: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature saying, "Come!"

R.5: When the Lamb opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature say, "Come!"

decisions.choice: the pattern repeats
decisions.reason: Each of the first four seals follows the same pattern: the Lamb opens a seal, one of the living creatures calls "Come!", and a horse and rider go out. See the notes on 6:1.

decisions.choice: the Lamb (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Lamb, who opens every seal (6:1).

records.source: καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος μέλας, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἔχων ζυγὸν ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And I saw, and behold a horse black, and the [one] sitting on it having a balance in the hand of him.
pieces: I looked, and there was a black horse, and the one who sat on it had a balance in his hand.

L.5: And I looked, and look, a black horse, and the one seated on it had a pair of scales in his hand.

R.5: I looked and saw a black horse. Its rider was holding scales for weighing food.

decisions.choice: a balance: scales for weighing food, a sign of scarcity
decisions.reason: ζυγὸν is a beam balance used in the market. When food was scarce it was weighed out carefully (compare Ezekiel 4:16, "they shall eat bread by weight and with anxiety"). The black horse brings famine.

decisions.choice: scales for weighing food (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the scales were for (m1).

records.source: καὶ ἤκουσα ὡς φωνὴν ἐν μέσῳ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων λέγουσαν· Χοῖνιξ σίτου δηναρίου, καὶ τρεῖς χοίνικες κριθῶν δηναρίου· καὶ τὸ ἔλαιον καὶ τὸν οἶνον μὴ ἀδικήσῃς.
records.gloss: And I heard as a voice in [the] middle of the four living creatures saying: A choenix of wheat of a denarius, and three choenixes of barley of a denarius; and the oil and the wine not harm.
pieces: And I heard what sounded like a voice among the four living creatures, saying: "A {{units:quart|choenix}} of wheat for {{units:a day's wages|a denarius}}, and three {{units:quarts|choenixes}} of barley for {{units:a day's wages|a denarius}}, but do not damage the olive oil and the wine!"

L.6: And I heard [something] like a voice in [the] middle of the four living creatures, saying, "A choenix of wheat for a denarius, and three choenixes of barley for a denarius, and do not harm the oil and the wine."

R.6: Then I heard something like a voice coming from among the four living creatures. It said, "Only one {{units:quart|choenix}} of wheat for {{units:a whole day's pay|a denarius}}, or three {{units:quarts|choenixes}} of barley for {{units:a whole day's pay|a denarius}}! But do not harm the olive oil and the wine."

decisions.choice: famine prices: a day's wage for a day's food
decisions.reason: A denarius was a laborer's pay for a day (Matthew 20:2). A choenix, a little over a quart, was about the grain one person ate in a day. The prices are many times the usual, so that a day's work buys bread for the worker alone, or cheaper barley for a small family. It describes severe scarcity, not starvation.

decisions.choice: spare the oil and the wine: a famine that is limited
alternatives: the rich keep their luxuries while the poor go hungry
decisions.reason: Olive trees and vines have deep roots and survive a drought that ruins a grain harvest. The command limits the famine: it is severe but not total. Some take oil and wine as luxuries, so that the famine hurts the poor most. The text does not say.

decisions.choice: something like a voice among the creatures
decisions.reason: The voice comes from the center of the four living creatures, where the throne and the Lamb are (4:6; 5:6). It is most likely the voice of God or the Lamb, setting limits to the judgment.

decisions.choice: units: quart, a day's wages
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek units. Balanced and Readable give modern equivalents, with "choenix" and "denarius" as the alternatives, so the reader can see what the prices meant (m1).

records.source: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν τετάρτην, ἤκουσα φωνὴν τοῦ τετάρτου ζῴου λέγοντος· Ἔρχου.
records.gloss: And when he opened the seal the fourth, I heard the fourth living creature saying: Come.
pieces: The Lamb broke the fourth seal, and I heard the fourth living creature say, "Come!"

L.7: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} opened the fourth seal, I heard the fourth living creature saying, "Come!"

R.7: When the Lamb opened the fourth seal, I heard the fourth living creature say, "Come!"

decisions.choice: the pattern repeats
decisions.reason: Each of the first four seals follows the same pattern: the Lamb opens a seal, one of the living creatures calls "Come!", and a horse and rider go out. See the notes on 6:1.

decisions.choice: the Lamb (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Lamb, who opens every seal (6:1).

records.source: καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος χλωρός, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ ὄνομα αὐτῷ ὁ Θάνατος, καὶ ὁ ᾅδης ἠκολούθει μετ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἐξουσία ἐπὶ τὸ τέταρτον τῆς γῆς, ἀποκτεῖναι ἐν ῥομφαίᾳ καὶ ἐν λιμῷ καὶ ἐν θανάτῳ καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν θηρίων τῆς γῆς.
records.gloss: And I saw, and behold a horse pale-green, and the [one] sitting upon it, name to him the Death, and the Hades was following with him, and was given to them authority over the fourth of the earth, to kill with sword and with famine and with death and by the beasts of the earth.
pieces: I looked, and I saw a horse the sickly green of a corpse. Death was the name of the one who sat on it, and Hades went along with him. To them was given power over a quarter of the earth, to kill with the sword, with hunger, with deadly disease, and by the earth's wild animals.

L.8: And I looked, and look, a pale green horse, and the one seated on it, his name [was] Death, and Hades followed with him, and authority was given to them over a fourth of the earth, to kill with sword and with famine and with death and by the wild animals of the earth.

R.8: I looked and saw a horse that was a sick, pale green color. The rider's name was Death. The place of the dead followed close behind him. They were given power over one fourth of the earth. They could kill people with war, hunger, disease, and wild animals.

decisions.choice: pale green: the color of a corpse
decisions.reason: χλωρός means the pale green of young plants, and also the greyish green of a sick or dead body. The fourth horse has the color of death.

decisions.choice: Death and Hades: death, and the realm of the dead that follows it
decisions.reason: Death and Hades appear together as powers in 1:18 and 20:13-14. Death takes life, and Hades receives the dead. On Hades see the note on 1:18.

decisions.choice: sword, famine, plague and wild beasts: Ezekiel's four judgments
decisions.reason: Ezekiel 14:21 names God's "four disastrous acts of judgment, sword, famine, wild beasts and plague". The second "death" in the list, θανάτῳ, means a deadly plague, as the same word does in the Greek of Ezekiel. The power is limited to a fourth of the earth.

decisions.choice: was given: God permits it
decisions.reason: "Was given" leaves the giver unnamed, but in Revelation it is God who allows the riders to act (compare 6:4, 8; 9:1-5; 13:5-7). Even the forces of war and death act only within the limits he sets.

decisions.choice: death (L); deadly disease (B); disease (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek word; Balanced and Readable say what it means here (m3).

decisions.choice: Hades (L, B); the place of the dead (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:18.

records.source: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν πέμπτην σφραγῖδα, εἶδον ὑποκάτω τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν ἐσφαγμένων διὰ τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ διὰ τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἣν εἶχον.
records.gloss: And when he opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of those having been slaughtered because of the word of the God and because of the testimony which they had.
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} opened the fifth seal, I saw beneath the altar the souls of those who had been slaughtered for the sake of the word of God and of the witness they held to.

L.9: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of those who had been slaughtered because of the word of God and because of the testimony that they held.

R.9: When the Lamb opened the fifth seal, I saw the souls of people under the altar. They had been killed because they were faithful to God's word and to the truth they had told.

decisions.choice: under the altar: their deaths seen as sacrifices
alternatives: under the altar of incense, where prayers rise (8:3-5)
decisions.reason: At the altar of sacrifice the blood of the victims was poured out at its base (Leviticus 4:7). Those killed for God's word are pictured there, as if their lives had been poured out to God (compare Philippians 2:17; 2 Timothy 4:6). The heavenly altar in 8:3-5 is an altar of incense, and the prayers of these souls may be the prayers that rise there.

decisions.choice: souls: the persons themselves, alive with God after death
decisions.reason: ψυχὰς means life or the living person. Here it is those who were killed, still living and speaking before God.

decisions.choice: the word of God and the testimony they held
decisions.reason: The phrase is the one used of John in 1:9. The testimony is the witness they held to and bore, most likely their witness to Jesus (12:17; 20:4).

decisions.choice: were faithful to God's word and to the truth they had told (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly why they were killed.

records.heading: The fifth seal: the souls under the altar

records.source: καὶ ἔκραξαν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγοντες· Ἕως πότε, ὁ δεσπότης ὁ ἅγιος καὶ ἀληθινός, οὐ κρίνεις καὶ ἐκδικεῖς τὸ αἷμα ἡμῶν ἐκ τῶν κατοικούντων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς;
records.gloss: And they cried out with a voice loud saying: Until when, the master the holy and true, not you judge and avenge the blood of us from those dwelling on the earth?
pieces: They cried out with a loud voice: "Holy and true Master, how long until {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} judge those who live on the earth and give justice for our blood?"

L.10: And they cried out with a loud voice, saying, "How long, holy and true Master, will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not judge and avenge our blood on those who live on the earth?"

R.10: They shouted, "Holy and true Lord, how much longer will it be before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} judge the people on earth? When will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} punish them for killing us?"

decisions.choice: holy and true Master: God, the sovereign owner of his slaves
decisions.reason: δεσπότης is the word for a master who owns slaves, used of God in prayer (Luke 2:29; Acts 4:24). It matches "fellow slaves" in 6:11. "Holy and true" is said of Christ in 3:7; here it is said to God.

decisions.choice: How long? The cry of the psalms for justice
decisions.reason: The psalms ask God how long he will let the wicked go unpunished (Psalm 79:5-10; 94:3), and Psalm 79:10 asks that the blood of his servants be avenged before the nations. Deuteronomy 32:43 says that God avenges the blood of his servants. The martyrs do not take revenge; they ask God to judge justly and leave it to him (compare Romans 12:19).

decisions.choice: those who live on the earth: the world that opposes God
decisions.reason: See the note on 3:10.

decisions.choice: Master (L, B); Lord (R)
decisions.reason: "Master" keeps the sense of the Greek (m1). Readable uses "Lord", which young readers know as a title of God.

records.source: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἑκάστῳ στολὴ λευκή, καὶ ἐρρέθη αὐτοῖς ἵνα ἀναπαύσονται ἔτι χρόνον μικρόν, ἕως πληρωθῶσιν καὶ οἱ σύνδουλοι αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτῶν οἱ μέλλοντες ἀποκτέννεσθαι ὡς καὶ αὐτοί.
records.gloss: And was given to them each a robe white, and it was said to them that they will rest yet a time little, until should be completed also the fellow-slaves of them and the brothers of them, those being about to be killed as also they.
pieces: A white robe was handed to each of them, and they were told to rest a short time more, until the number of their fellow servants and {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} was complete, those who were going to be killed as they had been.

L.11: And a white robe was given to each of them, and they were told to rest a little while longer, until [the number of] their fellow slaves and their {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} who were about to be killed as they [had been] should be complete.

R.11: Then each of them was given a white robe. They were told to rest a little longer. Others who were God's servants, their {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, would be killed as they had been. They must wait until the full number of them had died.

decisions.choice: a white robe: a sign of victory and purity
decisions.reason: See 3:4-5 and 7:9-14. The robe is God's answer before the full answer comes.

decisions.choice: until the number is complete: God has set a limit to the martyrs' suffering
decisions.reason: πληρωθῶσιν means "be filled" or "be completed". It most likely means that a number known to God must be completed before judgment comes (compare 4 Ezra 4:35-37, a Jewish writing of about John's time). Some manuscripts have a form that means "until they complete their course". The text does not say how many, or how long.

decisions.choice: fellow servants (B); others who were God's servants (R)
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it (1:1); Literal keeps "fellow slaves".

decisions.choice: brothers and sisters | brothers
decisions.reason: ἀδελφοὶ includes believers of both sexes, so it takes the gender setting.

records.source: Καὶ εἶδον ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν ἕκτην, καὶ σεισμὸς μέγας ἐγένετο, καὶ ὁ ἥλιος ἐγένετο μέλας ὡς σάκκος τρίχινος, καὶ ἡ σελήνη ὅλη ἐγένετο ὡς αἷμα, καὶ οἱ ἀστέρες τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἔπεσαν εἰς τὴν γῆν, ὡς συκῆ βάλλει τοὺς ὀλύνθους αὐτῆς ὑπὸ ἀνέμου μεγάλου σειομένη, καὶ ὁ οὐρανὸς ἀπεχωρίσθη ὡς βιβλίον ἑλισσόμενον, καὶ πᾶν ὄρος καὶ νῆσος ἐκ τῶν τόπων αὐτῶν ἐκινήθησαν.
records.gloss: And I saw when he opened the seal the sixth, and earthquake great happened, and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the moon whole became as blood, \v 13 and the stars of the heaven fell to the earth, as a fig tree casts the unripe figs of it by a wind great being shaken, \v 14 and the heaven was split off as a scroll being rolled up, and every mountain and island out of the places of them were moved.
pieces: Then I saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} open the sixth seal, and a great earthquake struck. The sun went as black as sackcloth made of hair, the full moon became like blood,
and the stars in the sky dropped to the earth, the way unripe figs drop from a fig tree when a gale shakes it.
The sky was torn away like a scroll that rolls itself up, and every mountain and island was shifted out of its place.

L.12: And I looked when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} opened the sixth seal, and a great earthquake took place, and the sun became black as sackcloth made of hair, and the whole moon became like blood,
L.13: and the stars of heaven fell to the earth, as a fig tree drops its unripe figs when shaken by a great wind,
L.14: and the sky was split apart like a scroll being rolled up, and every mountain and island was moved out of its place.

R.12: I watched the Lamb open the sixth seal. There was a powerful earthquake. The sun became completely dark, as black as rough black cloth. The whole moon turned as red as blood.
R.13: The stars fell from the sky to the earth. They fell like green figs that fall from a tree when a strong wind shakes it.
R.14: The sky disappeared like a scroll being rolled up. Every mountain and every island was moved from its place.

decisions.choice: the signs of the day of the Lord in the prophets
decisions.reason: The prophets describe God's day of judgment with the same pictures: the sun darkened and the moon turned to blood (Joel 2:10, 31), the stars falling like fruit from a fig tree and the sky rolled up like a scroll (Isaiah 34:4), the earth shaken (Isaiah 13:10-13; Haggai 2:6). Jesus used them of the end (Mark 13:24-25). Whether John means events in the sky, or uses the prophets' language for the collapse of the world's order before God, the scene is the coming of the great day of wrath (6:17).

decisions.choice: sackcloth: rough cloth of black goat hair, worn in mourning
decisions.reason: Sackcloth was a coarse cloth made of goat hair, usually black, and people wore it to mourn or repent (Isaiah 50:3, "I clothe the heavens with blackness and make sackcloth their covering").

decisions.choice: unripe figs: late figs that never ripen and fall in the winter wind
decisions.reason: ὀλύνθους are the figs that grow late in the season and drop when the winter winds shake the tree.

decisions.choice: sackcloth (L, B); rough black cloth (R)
decisions.reason: Readable describes the cloth, since few young readers know the word (m2).

records.heading: The sixth seal: the great day

records.source: καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς καὶ οἱ μεγιστᾶνες καὶ οἱ χιλίαρχοι καὶ οἱ πλούσιοι καὶ οἱ ἰσχυροὶ καὶ πᾶς δοῦλος καὶ ἐλεύθερος ἔκρυψαν ἑαυτοὺς εἰς τὰ σπήλαια καὶ εἰς τὰς πέτρας τῶν ὀρέων·
records.gloss: And the kings of the earth and the great ones and the commanders and the rich and the strong and every slave and free hid themselves in the caves and in the rocks of the mountains;
pieces: Then the earth's kings and its high officials, its military commanders, its wealthy and its powerful, and every slave and every free person, went into hiding in the caves and the mountain crags.

L.15: And the kings of the earth and the great ones and the commanders and the rich and the mighty and every slave and free [person] hid themselves in the caves and among the rocks of the mountains.

R.15: Everyone hid in caves and among the rocks in the mountains. Kings, rulers, army leaders, rich people, powerful people, slaves, and free people all hid.

decisions.choice: seven kinds of people: everyone, from the highest to the lowest
decisions.reason: The list runs from kings down to slaves and has seven members, the number of completeness. No rank or power protects anyone on this day.

decisions.choice: hiding in caves and rocks: Isaiah 2
decisions.reason: Isaiah 2:10, 19-21 says that people will enter the caves of the rocks and the holes of the ground from before the terror of the LORD, when he rises to shake the earth.

decisions.choice: the hiding first (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what happened first and then lists who did it, so that the long subject does not lose a young reader.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slave is set against free.

records.source: καὶ λέγουσιν τοῖς ὄρεσιν καὶ ταῖς πέτραις· Πέσετε ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς καὶ κρύψατε ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ καθημένου ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς ὀργῆς τοῦ ἀρνίου, ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ἡμέρα ἡ μεγάλη τῆς ὀργῆς αὐτῶν, καὶ τίς δύναται σταθῆναι;
records.gloss: And they say to the mountains and to the rocks: Fall on us and hide us from [the] face of the [one] sitting on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb, \v 17 because came the day the great of the wrath of them, and who is able to stand?
pieces: To the mountains and rocks they cry, "Fall on us! Cover us from the sight of the one seated on the throne, and from the Lamb's wrath!
For the great day of their wrath is here, and who is able to stand?"

L.16: And they say to the mountains and to the rocks, "Fall on us and hide us from [the] face of the one seated on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb,
L.17: for the great day of their wrath has come, and who is able to stand?"

R.16: They begged the mountains and the rocks, "Fall on us! Hide us from the one sitting on the throne. Hide us from the anger of the Lamb!
R.17: The great day when they show their anger has come. Who can survive it?"

decisions.choice: "Fall on us": Hosea 10:8, and Jesus's words on the way to the cross
decisions.reason: Hosea 10:8 says that people will say to the mountains, "Cover us", and to the hills, "Fall on us". Jesus quoted the words to the women of Jerusalem (Luke 23:30).

decisions.choice: the wrath of the Lamb
decisions.reason: The Lamb who was slaughtered (5:6) is also the judge. The phrase joins what seems impossible to join: gentleness and wrath. His wrath is not a loss of temper but his just judgment on those who refuse him.

decisions.choice: their wrath: the wrath of God and the Lamb
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads αὐτῶν, "their", joining God and the Lamb. Many manuscripts read "his". The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Who can stand? Joel and Malachi
decisions.reason: "The day of the LORD is great and very terrible; who can endure it?" (Joel 2:11; compare Malachi 3:2; Nahum 1:6). Chapter 7 answers the question: those whom God has sealed stand before the throne (7:9).

decisions.choice: wrath (L, B); anger (R)
decisions.reason: "Wrath" is the familiar word for God's judgment; Readable uses the plain word.
